name: oh-my-bb
description: Independent BB plugins maintained by Hemanth Soni.

plugins.description: Automate Brave with isolated logins, live viewing and manual handoff.
plugins.overview:
Browser gives each BB thread its own tabs. Sandbox sessions also have separate
profiles, so two threads can sign in to different accounts on the same site.
An optional extension can relay an explicitly paired regular profile, or export
cookies while that browser stays open. A toolbar popup shows connection and sync
health. Authentication sharing is off until enabled.

Watch a sandbox browser live inside chat. When a login, OAuth approval or bot
check needs you, the agent pauses and opens the same private desktop for direct
mouse and keyboard input. Finish with Done to resume. Browser chrome, dialogs
and popups stay in that session. Local handoffs ask for attention; they do not
switch your workspace or focus a window.

## Getting started

Install Browser in BB. For managed sandbox viewing and routing, also install
Sandboxes and enable **Enable Sandboxes integration** under Oh My BB.
Configure that plugin's provider and runtime image separately. Browser never
installs or probes it at startup. The `bb-browser` CLI must be installed on
the browser host; plugin startup does not change your command or profiles.

To use your regular profile, open Settings → Browser → More → Browser connection,
download the extension, load it unpacked in Brave or Chrome, and pair it.
The local browser remains open. Pairing does not enable cookie export by itself.

Home Tailscale routing and personal-login sharing are separate global choices.
Both and the Sandboxes integration are off on a fresh installation. Saved
routing, sharing and migrated integration choices remain enabled on upgrade
unless explicitly turned off. Home routing needs an exit node and reusable
enrollment key; it fails closed if unavailable. Login sharing seeds new isolated
sessions. Turning it off stops future sharing, not logins already in use.

Configuration holds keys and authentication-file inputs. Preferences holds
behavior. Connection controls and the collapsed setup guide are under More.

## Support and integrations

The managed native backend requires Linux, Brave, and Hyprland's Lua window-rule
API. Isolated headed sessions require Linux, TigerVNC or Xvfb, and Openbox; the
Sandboxes image supplies them. The regular-profile extension supports Chromium
browsers, not Firefox. Native process ownership checks are Linux-specific.
There is no claim of full macOS or Windows automation support.

Browser works without Sandboxes for local native and relay workflows. Sandboxes
adds cloud lifecycle, private remote viewing and home-network enrollment.
Pages is not a dependency; the extension carries its own theme assets.
Fast-model tasks are optional and off by default. They send page observations
to the configured provider only after explicit task authorization.

Use `bb-browser`, `browser_handoff` and `browser_live` from a BB thread.
See the package README for setup, commands and verification limits.

plugins.description: Retain scoped context, reusable lessons, and workflow feedback for BB agents.
plugins.overview:
# Clasi

Retain scoped context, reusable lessons, and workflow feedback for BB agents.

## Keep useful guidance

- **Context** stores generalized facts and preferences.
- **Napkins** store reusable situation/action lessons.
- **Papercuts** track fixable workflow friction through open, resolved, and dismissed states.

Use Everywhere, Repository, or This worktree scope. More specific guidance overrides the same logical key in broader scopes. Review records in the Clasi panel. Native Configuration controls the active instruction budget.

## Private by default

Records stay in BB's private plugin database. Clasi does not publish or synchronize them. It never copies raw conversations automatically. Retain only generalized guidance, not messages, source excerpts, paths, secrets, personal information, or customer data.

Instruction limits do not delete stored records. Papercut details stay in the review panel; agents receive only open severity counts.

## Optional integration

Clasi runs without other Oh My BB packages. Separately installed Pinpoint can save a proposed design or copy preference after explicit learning approval in its review flow. Approval without that opt-in writes nothing. Clasi never probes, installs, or enables Pinpoint.

## Requirements

BB 0.46.1 or later. No API key, external account, or paid model service is required by Clasi. Records and settings remain local to the BB server.

Drive BB by voice.

## What you get

Choose **Talk in app** from Dispatch in the sidebar footer, or press
Mod+Shift+H, and say what you want. The agent, Juno by default, keeps its answers short and acts first. It can:

- Tell you what is running, and read what a thread did last.
- Start a thread, send it a message, change its model, rename, stop, or
  archive it. It asks before it stops or archives one.
- Bring a thread or its diff on screen.
- Run commands from the plugins you allow.

While a call is live, it also tells you when a thread finishes or fails. The
footer pet shows what the agent is doing: listening, talking, reading, or working.

Pick a voice and play a short sample of it. Every listed voice has a
built-in sample in the default style, so it plays at once with no key. Set the voice style: pace,
energy, expressiveness, turn length, and backchannels. The style is a set of
sentences in the voice prompt, not an exact control. You can also design a
voice from a description.

The Dispatch console lists every call with its transcript, the tools it ran,
and the voice minutes it used.

Keep your keys in the native Configuration form. Choose how Dispatch works
under Preferences, including Plugin access for allowed commands. Open the setup
guide from More. Oh My BB links to the Webhooks-owned phone-event integration.

The agent remembers past calls. After each call, your reasoning model writes a
short summary with your OpenAI key. The agent sees your last few calls and your
local time, and can look up older ones. Summaries and transcripts stay in
Dispatch's database for 90 days by default. You can turn memory off, keep it
longer or shorter, or forget one call. Other plugins may read call summaries
through the read-only `read.calls` RPC. `bb dispatch` checks setup, stops or mutes the
call, and reports usage.

## Two modes

In-app voice needs only an OpenAI API key with GPT-Live access. Audio goes
straight from your browser to OpenAI.

Phone calls need a Twilio account and number, your phone number, an OpenAI
project id for SIP, and the Webhooks plugin to hear when a call arrives. You
get the same agent and the same tools, with no screen.

BB shows "Needs configuration" only when the OpenAI key is missing. After you
add it, Dispatch reloads itself.

## Cost

Voice time is estimated at $0.05 per minute. The reasoning model's tokens,
including call summaries, are billed by OpenAI on top and are not counted.
Phone calls also use Twilio minutes. Built-in voice samples are free. A new
sample, for your own voice or your style, costs about 1¢ and is not counted.

## Standalone by default

In-app voice needs no other BB plugin. Phone calls work only when the Webhooks
plugin is installed separately. Dispatch never installs or enables it.

Experimental Podcast mode adds project-specific people and voices, scoped
thread controls, and queued project updates in the app.
See [Podcast](docs/podcast.md).

plugins.description: Keep coding when a Claude or ChatGPT account reaches its limit.
plugins.overview:
Keep coding when a Claude or ChatGPT account reaches its limit. Supported BB
harnesses keep working across provider limits without moving a conversation to
another thread.

## What you get

Model Gateway gives Claude Code, Codex, omp, FX, nanocodex, Prime Agent, and Pi an ordered
chain of provider accounts and API-key fallbacks. A thread stays on its selected
upstream during a tool loop, then can return to the primary account on a later
turn after its limit resets. Early Responses stream capacity errors also fail
over before output reaches the harness. Capacity cooldowns back off to five
minutes; a new user turn checks recovery with its real request. There are no
background health probes.

Settings groups routes in Configuration, subscription access in Preferences,
and upstream accounts and keys in Credentials. Advanced holds model mappings
and limits. More opens the setup guide. The footer shows subscription account usage.
The optional Sandboxes plugin shows the current upstream and model in its
machine popover. The same gateway controls are available through `bb gateway`.

## Protocol translation

The gateway translates between Anthropic Messages and OpenAI Responses when a
fallback speaks a different protocol. Replay guards prevent reasoning or
thinking data created by one upstream from being sent to another upstream.

## Optional integrations

Claude Code and Codex work without another plugin or agent adapter. omp and Pi
use setup files generated by `bb gateway setup host`. Hempi and agent profiles
share Pi's chain and routing. FX, nanocodex, and Prime Agent use separate,
optional ACP adapters; Model Gateway neither installs nor requires them.
Routed FX and Prime Agent need no local provider login.

Standalone Pi on the BB server machine can use `bb gateway setup pi --standalone --machine <name>`.
It saves private credentials and requires BB to keep running. BB-managed sessions keep their own credentials.
Pi Fast mode supports gateway GPT models and supported Claude Opus models. Claude Fast mode uses paid usage credits. The gateway carries the speed setting across protocol fallbacks and preserves Claude’s reported speed.

Automatic model selection through Jev is optional. It sends the truncated last
user message and candidate model names to OpenRouter for each eligible turn.

## Requirements and costs

You provide the Claude, ChatGPT, or API-key accounts you choose to route. Claude
Max OAuth accounts may serve only Claude Code unless you opt in under Preferences. API-key fallbacks bill per token,
and Jev requires an OpenRouter API key. Model Gateway stores credentials in BB's
plugin data directory and never returns secret values through its CLI or UI.

Configured API accounts run automatically. Spending is governed by upstream billing and key protections; the gateway adds no approval gate.

plugins.description: A searchable journal of BB thread lifecycle and work history.
plugins.overview:
A searchable journal of BB thread lifecycle and work history.

## A journal that writes itself

Journal records thread creation, archival, restoration, and deletion without treating archive time as work time. Idle turns index provisional work days. Closed days from the last seven days can get one transcript-aware AI pass when enabled; a configurable $0.50/day automatic spend budget and 500-call backstop persist across reloads. An explicit, resumable all-time backfill can index older days after a read-only cost estimate without deleting earlier work-day rows.

## Catch up on any thread

Catch up in each thread's native three-dot menu opens a saved briefing: the original goal, what is done, what remains, where it stopped, and which decisions are made or still open, with live status and freshness. The action uses the Journal icon and is also available in native sidebar thread menus. Opening it never calls a model. With the optional subscription backend, Journal refreshes briefings in the background after a thread goes idle, through the Model Gateway's ChatGPT subscription accounts with no paid fallback.

## Designed for a real archive

The Journal page offers daily, weekly, and all-time replay with per-day outcomes, work-category filters, project breakdowns, and a separate lifecycle context. Visible child-agent and side-chat work rolls into the parent day with links, so it does not inflate counts. Hidden workers remain omitted. Test-category activity stays visible.

Calendar shows agent turns as time blocks. Time sheet groups agent hours by thread or project and copies them as CSV. Traces shows raw turns, failures, and input requests. Calendar and Time sheet deliberately use a wider day-column canvas; text views align with BB Settings.

Categories cover bug fixes, features, improvements, research, analysis, operations, content, planning, reviews, projects, and tests. Local title rules work without an API key; manual corrections win over model results. The work-day timezone defaults to America/New_York and is configurable for new indexing and explicit backfill.

## Dispatch calls, if you want them

An optional Dispatch integration shows voice-agent calls as a thin rail beside the agent blocks in the Calendar, with their own rows in Traces. It is off by default; the Calls toggle turns it on. Journal reads calls from Dispatch on demand and stores nothing. Calls never count toward agent hours.

## Settings with clear ownership

Native Configuration holds only the OpenRouter API key. Preferences holds summaries, models, budget, and timezone. More links to setup. Oh My BB holds the optional Model Gateway backend selector and Dispatch switch. Neither integration is required or probed at startup.

Existing non-secret settings import without resetting saved values. One finishing Journal reload removes their legacy native editors. `bb journal preferences` reads or changes these values; the API key keeps its native command and secret storage.

## CLI included

Use `bb journal list` for paginated work days, `bb journal list --lifecycle` for events, and `bb journal summary` for dated highlights. `bb journal brief <id>` reads a saved briefing; `--refresh` explicitly requests a model pass. `bb journal ai-status` reads backend readiness without a model request. `bb journal backfill --dry-run` estimates all-time coverage and cost before any AI calls. `bb journal backfill --limit 5` saves a cursor and resumes in bounded batches, with at most 100 daily AI attempts per invocation. `bb journal backfill --status` shows failed days, provider blocks, and today's automatic budget without sending work to a provider. `bb journal cost` reports token and spend totals. JSON output is available.

All data stays in the plugin's BB-managed SQLite database. API keys remain host-local; transcripts go to the configured AI backend (OpenRouter, or ChatGPT subscription through Model Gateway) only when intelligence is enabled.

plugins.description: Publish and share pages, with the same live UI in chat and on pages.
plugins.overview:
Turn an HTML or Markdown file into a durable artifact that reads naturally
inside BB. Pages keeps changed versions together, renders the result inline in
chat, and gives prior work a searchable home instead of leaving it buried in a
thread.

## What you get

Publish with the `page_publish` agent tool or `bb pages publish`. Pages accepts
workspace and thread-storage files, or a whole folder with `index.html` and its
images, styles, and linked pages. It follows stable keys across runs, and skips
duplicate versions when the bytes have not changed. Local images referenced by
path are embedded at publish, so a page stays self-contained when shared.

Organize artifacts into project folders such as `Reports/Weekly`. The Pages
library groups them by project and folder, while `page_browse` lets an agent
find earlier pages by project, folder, or title before updating them.

Pages renders Markdown and sandboxed HTML with a light/dark theme, interactive
data tables, and optional charts. Pages and chat components share one icon
set, MingCute, so icons look the same everywhere and unlike most interfaces.
In chat, a page shows as a compact card, or borderless and inline for a
single chart, table, or diagram. A page can be
shared through Here.now with restricted, password, or public-link access.
Sharing requires your own Here.now API key and explicit confirmation in BB.

To ask for changes, type a note in the page panel's feedback box. Pages sends it
to the thread with the page id, so the agent updates the same page as a new
version.

An agent can also ask questions with a form, right in the chat. When you send
it, the answers go to the thread as one message, each under the label you saw.
The form then stays locked as sent. Pick Edit answers to change them and send
again.

For small things that belong to one reply, an agent skips the page and writes
live UI right in its message: a few numbers, a short table, a bar or line
chart, tabs, code, a diff, or a question with choices and sliders. It draws
as the reply streams and uses BB's own colours and code viewers. Buttons send
to the thread, like page forms. The same components work on a published page
or shared site, read-only, with their data saved when you publish.

## Standalone by default

Pages needs BB 0.46.1 or later and no setup. Sharing (a Here.now API key) and map
tiles (a Mapbox token) are optional settings. Each shows its own status where you
use it: the Share popover says when the key is not set, and a map names the
missing token. Pages does not require another BB plugin. If PR Review is installed separately,
it can publish structured review documents and receive actions from their page
menus. That integration remains inactive otherwise.

## Highcharts requirement

Charts on pages and in chat use the bundled Highcharts runtime. Highcharts is not MIT licensed.
You must obtain and manage your own Highcharts license for your intended use;
installing Pages does not grant one. Highcharts loads only when a chart draws. See the [Highcharts license](https://www.highcharts.com/license).

plugins.description: Turn incoming webhooks into BB actions.
plugins.overview:
Connect an authenticated webhook sender to a fixed action in BB.

## Key features

- **Four actions:** message an existing thread, start a thread in a project, run a saved automation, or deliver declared fields to a receiver plugin.
- **Sender authentication:** Standard Webhooks signatures, Slack signatures, or bearer tokens, with secrets managed per endpoint.
- **Bounded input:** declare field paths, types, and limits. The payload cannot choose the target, permissions, or action.
- **Duplicate protection:** dedupe by webhook ID, a declared field, or body hash. Set per-endpoint body and request-rate limits.
- **Slack support:** Events API, slash commands, interactivity, URL verification, and prompt acknowledgement. Socket Mode is not supported.
- **Delivery controls:** pause endpoints, rotate secrets, inspect results, and send signed tests. Tests run the real action.
- **UI and CLI:** manage endpoints in Webhooks or with `bb webhooks`. Delivery records omit payload values; bearer tokens are stored as hashes.

## First-time setup

1. Keep BB running. Configure an agent and a thread or project for thread actions.
2. Provide a public HTTPS hostname with a tunnel or reverse proxy. Prefer the loopback listener so the rest of BB stays private.
3. Set Listener port and Public base URL in Settings → Webhooks.
4. Open Webhooks → Setup guide, create an endpoint, and copy its delivery URL and one-time secret into the sender. Slack uses its own app signing secret.
5. Send a real event and inspect Deliveries. A local signed test does not check public ingress.

Cloudflare is optional. Its named tunnels need a Cloudflare account, `cloudflared`, and a domain managed by Cloudflare. Caddy or another HTTPS proxy works instead. Webhooks does not install ingress software, configure DNS, or open router ports. BB Connect cannot receive provider callbacks because it requires an owner session.

## Optional integrations and limits

- Install and enable Automations for the automation action, then opt in under Settings → Webhooks → **Oh My BB**. It runs a saved prompt without webhook fields.
- For the plugin action, install and enable a receiver publishing `webhooks_receive`, then enable its integration under **Oh My BB**. The receiver owns its behavior and description. Direct thread actions need no other plugin.
- Fresh installs start with integrations off. Upgrades preserve integrations used by existing hooks. Disabling one stops its actions without deleting configuration or secrets.
- Slack acknowledges before the action runs. Failed actions are recorded but are not retried automatically.

[Full setup and ingress examples](https://github.com/hemaaanth/oh-my-bb/blob/main/plugins/webhooks/docs/ingress.md)

plugins.description: Run bb.json commands and track services from thread actions.
Group BB threads by working status with nested thread summaries and saved ordering.
plugins.overview:
# Status Sidebar

Group BB threads by working status with nested thread summaries and saved ordering.

## See what needs attention

Group threads by status, workspace, or project. Combine a subgroup with recent, status, or manual ordering. Needs input, active work, drafting, unread, idle, and Later have distinct meanings. Parent summaries include the neediest child. Expand children without leaving the thread list.

BB keeps its navigation rail, footer, split navigation, keyboard targets, and native thread action menus. Status Sidebar adds a private Later marker. It does not replace BB's project or thread lifecycle controls. The sidebar stays narrow; its collapsible setup guide lives in plugin settings, not a separate rail page.

## Works alone

Native BB thread, project, draft, host, and navigation data power the base sidebar. Saved local groups, manual order, and collapse preferences remain available. No account, API key, or sibling package is required. Private state stays on the BB server or in the current client's browser storage.

## Optional integrations

Explicit Oh My BB switches in plugin settings enable Agents, Projects, or Tasks. Agents adds Bots and Channels. Projects supplies shared project groups and project order. Tasks adds query-driven attachment to an existing task. Install and configure each owner separately. All opt-ins default to off. Status Sidebar never installs, enables, or probes siblings at startup. Disabling an integration retains saved state. Previously saved native flags import once; one explicit reload finishes moving their controls to Oh My BB without duplicate editors.

## Requirements

BB 0.46.1 or later. Choose Status Sidebar under Settings → Appearance → Sidebar. Expand More → Setup guide in Status Sidebar's plugin settings. Native Thread list preferences are not rewritten.

plugins.description: Sync and manage Akiflow, Linear, and GitHub tasks.
plugins.overview:
# Tasks

Sync and manage Akiflow, Linear, and GitHub tasks.

## Plan work

- Put urgent tasks in Now and high-priority work in Later.
- Open project cards for other tasks. Drag to arrange or move work between projects.
- Keep stable provider identifiers, linked references, ownership, and source destinations.
- Attach existing BB chats or explicitly start new work. Chat state updates without Status Sidebar.
- Use native task mentions, agent tools, or `bb worktasks`.

## Configure

Enter keys in native Configuration. In Preferences, enable each app and choose Akiflow projects or Inbox, GitHub repositories, and Linear teams or projects to sync. Map selected sources to BB projects. The inline **More → Setup guide** covers setup, write permissions, printing, and saved state.

Provider changes and agent changes have separate controls. Agent changes start off. Akiflow uses a private web API that can change without notice. Provider selections, credentials, and existing task data remain private to the installation.

Akiflow's client identifier stays in private installation storage. An existing installation must preserve that identity during cutover; new installations generate their own. The package does not ship a shared device identifier.

## Optional integrations

Tasks runs without any suite plugins. Task chats use native BB threads. Status Sidebar owns its own Attach to task opt-in. Tasks uses native BB projects and never installs, enables, or probes another plugin at startup.

An optional receipt printer uses your configured HTTPS endpoint and existing print API key. Printing sends urgent task titles only after you press Print Now. No server is supplied.

## Requirements

BB 0.46.1 or later and Plugin SDK 0.6.49 or later. Each provider needs its own account and credential. Install and build from this package directory. No repository-root runtime dependencies are required.

plugins.description: Share temporary password-protected BB session viewers through Cloudflare Tunnel.
plugins.overview:
Give another person a temporary, password-protected view of a BB session without exposing BB's server.

## Share a conversation

Open Session Share beside Scripts in a thread's **⋯ menu**. A compact dialog offers Conversation or Pinpoint review and a duration. Your configured custom hostname is used automatically; otherwise, Session Share uses a temporary hostname. An active Pinpoint preview selects Review by default. If Pinpoint is inactive, open it manually before choosing Review. Conversation mode renders the session in a separate guest viewer. Choose an expiry or revoke access yourself. Send the URL and access code privately. Anyone with both can unlock the viewer. Guest sessions expire within four hours or at share expiry, whichever comes first.

## Review an app

Optional Review mode requires a separately installed Pinpoint with guest-preview isolation contract v1. Guests can capture feedback, reply and delete their own still-held captures. Captures and replies stay held until the owner explicitly releases them in Pinpoint. Guests cannot approve, dispatch or submit learning.

Reviewed apps run in opaque sandboxed previews. BB and guest cookies, Authorization headers and plugin tokens are not forwarded. Incompatible older Pinpoint output fails closed. View works without Pinpoint. Session Share never installs or enables another plugin.

## Requirements and private state

Requires BB 0.46.1 or newer, Node 22.15 or newer, and cloudflared installed on the BB server. Cloudflare Tunnel carries the connection. A custom hostname needs an existing named tunnel and its account configuration. Session Share does not install cloudflared or change ingress. A fresh install starts no tunnel. No paid model service is required.

Use native Configuration for tunnel settings. Setup help starts collapsed under More > Setup guide. Access codes remain in the local plugin database so the owner can copy them again. Protect that database and its backups as credentials.

plugins.description: Point at a live page and send reviewable visual feedback to BB agents.
plugins.overview:
# Pinpoint

Point at a live page and send reviewable visual feedback to BB agents.

## Point, ask, and review

Pick an element, select text, or edit rendered copy. Pinpoint keeps the page location, conversation, optional screenshot, and review state. Agents report changes as ready. You approve or reply with more feedback. Text edits retain an explicit confirmation step.

Open Pinpoint from a thread's panel launcher. Native Configuration controls the default URL, review-chat routing, and immediate dispatch. More → Setup guide explains the workflow and privacy boundaries.

## Optional integrations

Pinpoint works without other Oh My BB packages. Explicit opt-ins under Oh My BB can use saved Agents profiles, Provider Usage capacity checks, and Clasi learning. No integration is probed, installed, or enabled at startup.

Clasi learning requires both the global opt-in and approval of the exact text on an unchecked-by-default card. Approving the fix alone saves nothing to Clasi. Disabling blocks writes and retries without deleting existing choices.

## Private feedback

Source distribution does not publish comments, screenshots, settings, or approvals. Shared-review consumers own guest authentication, scope, expiry, CSRF, and allowed actions. Guest learning approval is not accepted by the standalone client.

Guest comments wait in a separate Guest feedback view. The owner can edit the pending text before approving it for agent processing with the checkmark. Later guest comments wait for fresh owner approval. Agent feedback counts only finished agent work awaiting review. Sharing and global immediate dispatch do not grant guest agent, completion, or learning authority. Guest controls are limited to capture, reply, and deletion of their own feedback before owner adoption.

Preview pages run in an opaque sandbox without BB login cookies. Actions requested inside the page need confirmation in BB. The resource bridge is limited to the selected app. Protected Connect URLs, sign-in flows, write APIs, and undeclared external services may not work. Older Session Share preview servers must adopt isolation contract version 1 before their embedded previews can load.

## Requirements

BB 0.46.1 or later. No required suite plugin, external account, or additional API key. The thread's configured agent may have its normal provider costs.
